name: Six-Pack in 30 Days
goal: 30 days of focused core training — planks, crunch and leg-raise progressions, plus short cardio finishers. Straight talk: you cannot spot-reduce fat, and 30 days of core work alone will not reveal abs. This builds the muscle and burns real calories; the deficit from your food log is what uncovers it.

name: 14-Day Belly Burn
goal: Two weeks of high-intensity intervals paired with core strength work. Be clear on the science: you cannot spot-reduce belly fat, and no exercise burns fat from one specific place. What this does is stack big calorie burns against a stronger core — the deficit from your food log is what actually shifts the fat.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Hard intervals need recovery. Walk, hydrate, log your meals.

sessions.title: Sprint Intervals
sessions.notes: Week 1: 3 hard efforts with full recovery. No open ground? Use stairs.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. The food log does the deficit work today.

sessions.title: Full Burn Finisher

sessions.title: HIIT + Core

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. The food log does the deficit work today.

name: Lose Weight in 30 Days
goal: A 30-day progressive cardio build: brisk and incline walking in week 1, jogging and cycling through weeks 2–3, running and rope intervals by week 4, with two rest days every week. The program creates the burn — your daily food log creates the deficit, so log every meal.

sessions.title: Base Walk
sessions.notes: Week 1: build the habit first. Conversational pace the whole way.

sessions.title: Incline Walk
sessions.notes: Week 1: find a hill, or set the treadmill to a 5–8% incline.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Rest days matter as much as the walks. Log every meal.

sessions.title: Long Walk
sessions.notes: Week 1: your longest walk of the week. Podcast recommended.

sessions.title: Walk + Strength
sessions.notes: Week 1: walk first, then two easy rounds of bodyweight work.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Weigh in tomorrow if you track weight.

sessions.title: Weekend Walk
sessions.notes: Week 1: same route, try to beat last time by a couple of minutes.

sessions.title: Jog Intervals
sessions.notes: Week 2: alternate 2 min jog / 2 min walk for the whole session.

sessions.title: Cycle Steady
sessions.notes: Week 2: steady spin. No bike? Do the incline walk instead.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Recovery day. Your deficit comes from the food log — keep it honest.

sessions.title: Incline Walk
sessions.notes: Week 2: uphill work builds the engine without the joint load.

sessions.title: Jog + Core
sessions.notes: Week 2: finish the jog, then three rounds of core.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Sleep is a weight-loss tool too.

sessions.title: Long Walk
sessions.notes: Week 2: long and easy. This is your highest-burn session.

sessions.title: Jog Intervals
sessions.notes: Week 3: alternate 2 min jog / 2 min walk for the whole session.

sessions.title: Cycle Steady
sessions.notes: Week 3: steady spin. No bike? Do the incline walk instead.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Recovery day. Your deficit comes from the food log — keep it honest.

sessions.title: Incline Walk
sessions.notes: Week 3: uphill work builds the engine without the joint load.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Sleep is a weight-loss tool too.

sessions.title: Long Walk
sessions.notes: Week 3: long and easy. This is your highest-burn session.

sessions.title: Run
sessions.notes: Week 4: continuous run at a pace you can just about hold.

sessions.title: Run

sessions.title: Rope Intervals

name: 14-Day Kegel & Core Power
goal: Two weeks of pelvic-floor training paired with deep core work — Kegel holds, bridges, planks and leg raises. This one is about control, continence and core stability, not calories: the kcal per session are deliberately tiny and that is exactly right. If you have pelvic pain or recent surgery, check with a clinician first.

sessions.title: Pelvic Floor Basics
sessions.notes: Week 1: 3 sets of 10 Kegels, 5 s each. Breathe normally — never bear down, and keep glutes and thighs relaxed.

sessions.title: Deep Core
sessions.notes: Week 1: pair each squeeze with a slow exhale. Rest as long as you hold.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: The pelvic floor is a muscle and needs recovery. Full rest today.

sessions.title: Control & Stability
sessions.notes: Week 1: quality over count — end the set when the squeeze weakens.

sessions.title: Endurance Holds
sessions.notes: Week 1: longer holds today — 7 s each, drop reps if needed.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Consistency beats intensity with this one.

sessions.title: Full Core Integration
sessions.notes: Week 1: hold a gentle Kegel through the plank — that is the whole point.

sessions.title: Pelvic Floor Basics
sessions.notes: Week 2: 4 sets of 12 Kegels, 8 s each. Breathe normally — never bear down, and keep glutes and thighs relaxed.

sessions.title: Deep Core
sessions.notes: Week 2: pair each squeeze with a slow exhale. Rest as long as you hold.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: The pelvic floor is a muscle and needs recovery. Full rest today.

sessions.title: Control & Stability
sessions.notes: Week 2: quality over count — end the set when the squeeze weakens.

sessions.title: Endurance Holds
sessions.notes: Week 2: longer holds today — 10 s each, drop reps if needed.

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Consistency beats intensity with this one.

sessions.title: Full Core Integration
sessions.notes: Week 2: hold a gentle Kegel through the plank — that is the whole point.

name: 21-Day Push-Up Power
goal: Three weeks of push-up progressions — volume, tempo, ladders and a weekly max test — backed by dips, bear crawls, planks and shadow-boxing warm-ups. Track your max set each week; that number is the whole scoreboard. No equipment needed.

sessions.notes: Week 1: 4 sets of 8. Knees down is a valid regression — full range always beats a sloppy rep.

sessions.title: Tempo Push

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Pushing muscles want 48 h. Rest properly.

sessions.title: Push Ladder

sessions.title: Conditioning Push

sessions.title: Rest day
sessions.notes: Second rest day. Protein and sleep do the rebuilding.

sessions.title: Max Test
sessions.notes: Week 1: one all-out set to failure, then 3 back-off sets. Write the number down — it should climb every week.

sessions.title: Conditioning Push
sessions.notes: Week 2: circuit, 5 rounds, minimal rest.

sessions.title: Max Test
